rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Cells divide by amitosis, mitosis or meiosis. The cell cycle (G1, S, G2, M) is regulated by checkpoints. Mitosis produces two genetically identical diploid cells for growth, repair and asexual reproduction. Meiosis halves the chromosome number and, through crossing over and independent assortment, generates the genetic diversity needed for sexual reproduction.…

rows.label: Formula
rows.text:
Mitosis: 2n parent → 2 daughter cells of 2n
Meiosis: 2n parent → 4 gametes of n
Crossing over adds to independent assortment → variation

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: Mitosis maintains the chromosome number (2n → 2n); meiosis halves it (2n → n).  ·  Crossing over and independent assortment occur in MEIOSIS only, not mitosis.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: NEB often asks for labelled mitosis diagrams plus a mitosis/meiosis comparison table.  ·  Mention the G1/S/G2/M checkpoints and their role in preventing cancer.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: Onion root-tip cells show classic mitotic figures.  ·  Human spermatogenesis (1 primary → 4 sperm) and oogenesis (1 primary → 1 ovum + 3 polar bodies).

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: Sister chromatids separate in Anaphase of mitosis and in Anaphase II of meiosis; homologous chromosomes separate in Anaphase I.  ·  Meiosis produces 4 haploid cells; mitosis produces 2 diploid cells.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: Label all 4 mitotic phases  ·  Mitosis vs meiosis table

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: PMAT = Prophase, Metaphase, Anaphase, Telophase.  ·  MITO = two identical cells (2n); MEI = 4 different gametes (n).

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: How is the anaphase of meiosis I different from that of mitosis?  ·  Explain why meiosis produces genetic variation.

rows.label: Hints
rows.text: Draw and label all four mitotic phases.  ·  Tabulate mitosis vs meiosis (6 points).

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: Cell cycle phases  ·  PMAT  ·  Crossing over  ·  Independent assortment

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Mitosis = growth, repair, asexual reproduction; meiosis = gametes + variation.  ·  PMAT is the mnemonic for mitotic phases.  ·  Crossing over (Prophase I) and independent assortment create variation.  ·  S phase doubles DNA; G2 prepares; checkpoints control entry to M.

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: A human cell with 46 chromosomes yields two daughter cells with 46 chromosomes after mitosis and four with 23 after meiosis.  ·  Cancer is essentially uncontrolled mitosis due to failed checkpoints.

rows.label: More practice
rows.text: What would happen if the S phase did not occur?  ·  Differentiate amitosis, mitosis and meiosis (3 points each).  ·  Define non-disjunction and give one disease example.

rows.label: More hints
rows.text: Explain how meiosis creates variation (two mechanisms).  ·  Describe cell-cycle checkpoints and the cause of cancer.

rows.label: Extra solved
rows.text: Down syndrome results from trisomy-21 non-disjunction.

rows.label: MCQ drill
rows.text: The number of daughter cells produced by meiosis is: → B  ·  Crossing over occurs during: → B

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: Cell cycle: interphase (G1 growth, S DNA replication, G2 preparation) + M phase (mitosis).  ·  Amitosis (direct division): simple splitting of the nucleus; rare, seen in some fungi and liver cells.  ·  Mitosis: one division producing two genetically identical diploid (2n) daughter cells; phases — prophase, metaphase, anaphase, telophase (PMAT).

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Checkpoints  ·  Non-disjunction  ·  Cancer

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Significance of meiosis  ·  Meiosis has two divisions (I & II); mitosis one.  ·  Mitotic errors → cancer; meiotic errors → aneuploidy (trisomy).

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: G2 is not a resting phase; DNA has already doubled in S, cells grow in G1.  ·  Non-disjunction means a pair fails to separate; it can happen in meiosis I or II.  ·  Define non-disjunction with a human example (trisomy 21).

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Learn the PMAT sequence and draw each phase from memory.  ·  Keep a mitosis vs meiosis comparison table.  ·  Memorise that crossing over occurs in Prophase I of meiosis.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Relate checkpoint failure to cancer and non-disjunction to aneuploidy.  ·  Mitosis maintains a species' diploid chromosome number.  ·  Meiosis is essential for sexual reproduction because it halves the genome.
